answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label email and retention marketing means MMC builds and runs your client's lifecycle messaging while you own the relationship. That covers welcome and abandoned-cart flows, post-purchase and win-back sequences, campaigns and segmentation across email, SMS and WhatsApp, in the tools the client already uses.

stages.breaks: The first message goes out generic.
stages.why: A new customer decides quickly if the brand feels like theirs, and a stock email does not.
stages.does: We write the welcome flow in the client's voice and check the first message before anything else.

stages.why: Between delivery and reorder, nothing reminds the customer the brand exists.
stages.does: Delivery, review requests and usage tips are scheduled, with copy you can read before launch.

stages.why: A reminder too early annoys, and one too late misses the reorder.
stages.does: We time reminders to how long the product lasts as the client describes it, then adjust on what the data shows.

stages.breaks: Win-back arrives after the customer has gone.
stages.why: By the time a discount appears, the customer has moved on.
stages.does: Quiet customers are caught earlier by a sequence, with the offer agreed with the client first.

stages.why: One campaign to the whole list teaches it to ignore the client.
stages.does: Segments from purchase and browsing decide who gets which message, and the report is cut the same way.
